name: Tyrannosaurus Rex
fact: The apex predator of the Cretaceous, with a bite force over 35,000 newtons — stronger than any other known land animal.

name: Triceratops
fact: Its skull could be up to a third of its total body length. The frill may have flushed with color for display rather than defense.

name: Velociraptor
fact: Far smaller than Jurassic Park depicted — roughly turkey-sized and covered in feathers. Its sickle claw pinned prey rather than slashing.

name: Brachiosaurus
fact: Unlike most sauropods, its front legs were longer than its hind legs, giving it a giraffe-like posture to browse the tallest treetops.

name: Stegosaurus
fact: Its diamond-shaped back plates were likely used for temperature regulation and display. Its brain was roughly the size of a walnut.

name: Ankylosaurus
fact: The armored tank of the Cretaceous. Its bony tail club could swing fast enough to break the ankles and legs of a T. Rex.

name: Spinosaurus
fact: A massive sail-backed predator. It is recognized as the largest known carnivorous dinosaur.

name: Pteranodon
fact: Technically a pterosaur, not a dinosaur. With a 7-meter wingspan, it soared over Cretaceous seas scooping fish like a giant pelican.

name: Diplodocus
fact: One of the longest dinosaurs ever. It had a whip-like tail used for communication or defense.

name: Allosaurus
fact: The apex predator of the Jurassic period. It was smaller but faster than the T. Rex.

name: Dilophosaurus
fact: Famous for its twin head crests. Pop culture falsely gave it a venom-spitting neck frill.

name: Parasaurolophus
fact: The duck-billed dinosaur. Known for the long, curved hollow crest on the back of its head.

name: Apatosaurus
fact: The massive sauropod famously known for decades by its scientific mix-up name, "Brontosaurus."

name: Pachycephalosaurus
fact: The bone-headed dinosaur. It featured a thick dome of solid bone on top of its skull.

name: Carnotaurus
fact: The "meat-eating bull." Known for the two distinct horns protruding from above its eyes.

name: Iguanodon
fact: One of the first dinosaurs ever discovered. Easily identified by its sharp spike-like thumbs.

name: Therizinosaurus
fact: The bizarre herbivore with giant claws. Its scythe-like claws grew up to three feet long.

name: Giganotosaurus
fact: A massive South American predator. It was roughly the same size as, or slightly larger than, the T. Rex.

name: Compsognathus
fact: The tiny, chicken-sized carnivore. It was long used as the benchmark for the smallest dinosaur.

name: Deinonychus
fact: Its 1964 discovery started the Dinosaur Renaissance, proving dinosaurs were agile, active, and likely warm-blooded.

name: Argentinosaurus
fact: A candidate for the heaviest land animal ever. A single vertebra stood over 1.5 meters tall.

name: Baryonyx
fact: Fossil evidence included fish scales inside its ribcage. Its long, narrow snout and hook-like claws were perfect for riverside fishing.

name: Archaeopteryx
fact: The iconic transitional fossil between dinosaurs and birds, showing both feathers and reptilian features like teeth and a bony tail.

name: Oviraptor
fact: Its name means 'egg thief,' but it was wrongly accused. The eggs it was found with were actually its own — it was a devoted parent.

name: Gallimimus
fact: Built for speed, it could likely run at 50 km/h. Featured in Jurassic Park as the stampeding herd seen by the main characters.

name: Styracosaurus
fact: Its frill was ringed with long bony spikes, making its head display one of the most dramatic of any dinosaur.

name: Maiasaura
fact: The 'good mother lizard.' Fossils of nests, eggs, and juveniles showed it raised its young in colonies — a landmark discovery in 1978.

name: Coelophysis
fact: One of the earliest dinosaurs. Hundreds of fossils were found together at Ghost Ranch, New Mexico — possibly a single mass death event.

name: Patagotitan
fact: Discovered in 2014, it rivals Argentinosaurus as the heaviest dinosaur ever. Its femur alone stood taller than an average person.

name: Quetzalcoatlus
fact: Named after the Aztec feathered serpent god. With a 10–12 meter wingspan, it is the largest flying creature ever known to have lived.

name: Microraptor
fact: A crow-sized feathered dinosaur with flight feathers on all four limbs. It likely glided between trees in Cretaceous forests.

name: Troodon
fact: Had some of the largest eyes relative to body size of any dinosaur, suggesting excellent night vision and high intelligence.

name: Albertosaurus
fact: A smaller cousin of T. Rex living 10 million years earlier. Fossil sites with multiple individuals suggest it may have hunted in packs.

name: Tarbosaurus
fact: The Asian equivalent of T. Rex, nearly identical in build. Its arms were proportionally even smaller than its famous relative.

name: Herrerasaurus
fact: One of the earliest known dinosaurs. Its classification was debated for decades — it shows a mix of primitive and advanced features.

name: Ceratosaurus
fact: One of the first large predators with a nose horn. Its four-fingered hands set it apart from the three-fingered theropods that followed.

name: Kentrosaurus
fact: Its back plates gave way to long spikes over the hips and tail, making it dangerous for any predator attempting to grab its hindquarters.

name: Protoceratops
fact: Famous for the 'fighting dinosaurs' fossil — a specimen found locked in combat with a Velociraptor, preserved mid-struggle in the Gobi Desert.

name: Edmontosaurus
fact: A primary prey item for T. Rex. Some fossils have healed bite marks matching T. Rex teeth, proof that victims sometimes survived the attack.

name: Yutyrannus
fact: A large feathered tyrannosaur. Its discovery proved that even big tyrannosaurs could have a coat of filamentous feathers in cold climates.

name: Corythosaurus
fact: Its hollow crest could produce low-frequency sounds, possibly allowing it to communicate across vast distances through dense forests.

name: Suchomimus
fact: Its 1-meter thumb claw and crocodile-like narrow skull were ideal for hooking fish from the rivers of Cretaceous northern Africa.

name: Carcharodontosaurus
fact: Named after the great white shark for its serrated teeth. One of the largest carnivores ever discovered, possibly rivaling T. Rex in size.

name: Majungasaurus
fact: The only confirmed cannibal dinosaur. Its bones show tooth marks matching its own species, likely feeding on dead members of its kind.

name: Abelisaurus
fact: Known from only a partial skull. Its stubby arms were even more vestigial than a T. Rex, with almost no functional fingers at all.

name: Saltasaurus
fact: The armored sauropod. Its discovery proved that even giant long-necked dinosaurs could have bony plates embedded in their skin.

name: Amargasaurus
fact: Had two rows of tall spines along its neck and back, possibly supporting a sail-like skin structure used for display or thermoregulation.

name: Nigersaurus
fact: A 'vacuum-cleaner' sauropod. Its wide, flat snout held over 500 tiny teeth in a single row, replaced every 14 days for mowing low plants.

name: Afrovenator
fact: One of the few large predators known from Jurassic Africa. Its teeth and claws suggest it hunted the giant sauropods sharing its ecosystem.

name: Megalosaurus
fact: The first dinosaur ever formally named and described, by William Buckland in 1824. Its name means 'great lizard.'

name: Euoplocephalus
fact: One of the most complete ankylosaurid skeletons ever found. Even its eyelids were armored with bony plates.

name: Nodosaurus
fact: An ankylosaur without a tail club. It relied purely on its dense mosaic of bony scutes for defense against large predators.

name: Sauropelta
fact: One of the most heavily armored nodosaurs, with long shoulder spines to deter predators from biting down on its flanks.

name: Psittacosaurus
fact: One of the most commonly found dinosaur fossils in Asia, with over 400 specimens ranging from hatchling to adult.

name: Pentaceratops
fact: Its skull is one of the largest of any known land animal. Two of its five 'horns' were actually enlarged cheekbones.

name: Chasmosaurus
fact: Its enormous frill had large openings covered by skin, keeping it lightweight. It was almost certainly used for colorful display.

name: Torosaurus
fact: Some paleontologists believe it may be a mature form of Triceratops, its skull changing dramatically as it aged — a hotly debated topic.

name: Zuniceratops
fact: The oldest ceratopsian from North America with brow horns, bridging the gap between small Asian relatives and later giants like Triceratops.

name: Heterodontosaurus
fact: The 'different-toothed lizard.' It had three types of teeth — cutting, grinding, and fang-like canines — highly unusual for an herbivore.

name: Hypsilophodon
fact: Once wrongly thought to be a tree-climber. It was certainly one of the fastest small herbivores, relying on speed over armor for defense.

name: Tenontosaurus
fact: Best known as Deinonychus prey. Multiple Deinonychus skeletons have been found alongside Tenontosaurus bones at the same feeding sites.

name: Camptosaurus
fact: A versatile ornithopod that could walk on two or four legs. Its thumb spikes may have been used for foraging or light defense.

name: Dryosaurus
fact: A fast, bipedal herbivore built for speed. It relied on flight as its primary defense, with long legs and a stiff tail for balance.

name: Muttaburrasaurus
fact: One of Australia's most famous dinosaurs. Its large, bulbous nasal dome may have been used to amplify calls or for species recognition.

name: Minmi
fact: The smallest known ankylosaur. One Minmi specimen is the most complete dinosaur skeleton ever found in Australia.

name: Atlascopcosaurus
fact: Named after Atlas Copco, the company that supplied the equipment used to excavate it from a sea cave in Victoria, Australia.

name: Tsintaosaurus
fact: Famous for its controversial crest, once thought to be a unicorn-like spike. New fossils confirmed it had a genuine forward-pointing head crest.

name: Saurolophus
fact: Fossils have been found in both North America and Asia, making it one of the very few dinosaur species confirmed on two continents.

name: Lambeosaurus
fact: Had a hatchet-shaped hollow crest that served as a resonating chamber for calls and a visual signal to identify its own species.

name: Gryposaurus
fact: The 'hook-nosed lizard.' It had hundreds of tightly packed teeth — one of the most efficient plant-processing mouths of any dinosaur.

name: Sinornithosaurus
fact: One of the first feathered dinosaurs found in China. Some researchers controversially suggested it may have had grooved, venom-delivering teeth.

name: Guanlong
fact: An early tyrannosaur from Jurassic China with an elaborate head crest. It shows what the ancestors of T. Rex looked like 160 million years ago.

name: Dilong
fact: A small, feathered tyrannosaur. Its discovery provided key evidence that the T. Rex lineage began small and feathered before growing massive.

name: Alioramus
fact: A gracile tyrannosaur with a notably long, narrow skull and a row of small bumps along its snout, very unlike the robust T. Rex build.

name: Nanuqsaurus
fact: The 'polar bear lizard.' A small tyrannosaur that lived above the Arctic Circle, proving dinosaurs could thrive in cold, dark polar winters.

name: Daspletosaurus
fact: A direct ancestor candidate of T. Rex. It was nearly as large and illustrates the tyrannosaur lineage growing progressively bigger over time.

name: Gorgosaurus
fact: Fossil evidence suggests juveniles had different diets than adults — a form of ecological age separation to reduce competition within the species.

name: Eoraptor
fact: One of the earliest dinosaurs, from 231 million years ago. Its simple teeth suggest omnivory at the very base of the dinosaur family tree.

name: Plateosaurus
fact: One of the first large dinosaurs, found in hundreds of fossils across Europe. It walked upright and could rear up to browse high vegetation.

name: Riojasaurus
fact: An early prosauropod from Argentina that walked on all fours, unlike its bipedal relatives, foreshadowing the giant sauropod body plan.

name: Camarasaurus
fact: The most commonly found sauropod in North America. Its spoon-shaped teeth were tougher than most sauropods', able to process coarser vegetation.

name: Supersaurus
fact: One of the longest dinosaurs ever found, possibly exceeding 33 meters from nose to tail. Its sheer size made it nearly predator-proof.

name: Mamenchisaurus
fact: Famous for the longest neck of any dinosaur relative to body size — nearly half its total length. Used to browse otherwise unreachable vegetation.

name: Omeisaurus
fact: A large Chinese sauropod with a club-like tail tip. It lived in herds browsing the lush forests of Jurassic China.

name: Jobaria
fact: A surprisingly primitive sauropod for its age. Its anatomy barely changed for millions of years, suggesting a highly successful body plan.

name: Rapetosaurus
fact: Known from an exceptionally complete juvenile skeleton. The baby shows sauropods were independent from birth, receiving no parental care.

name: Dreadnoughtus
fact: Named after the battleship for being nearly impervious when alive. One of the most complete giant sauropod skeletons ever excavated.

name: Magyarosaurus
fact: A dwarf sauropod from a Cretaceous island. Its island-dwelling population shrank dramatically over generations — a phenomenon called insular dwarfism.

name: Irritator
fact: Named for the frustration paleontologists felt when they discovered the fossil had been extended with plaster by fossil dealers before sale.

name: Concavenator
fact: The 'hump-backed hunter of Cuenca.' Two elongated vertebrae formed a small hump or sail, possibly used for display or fat storage.

name: Scipionyx
fact: The best-preserved theropod ever found in Italy, with soft tissue including intestines, trachea, and liver intact for 113 million years.

name: Wuerhosaurus
fact: One of the last known stegosaurs, surviving 20 million years longer than most of its family. Its plates were flatter and more rounded.

name: Tuojiangosaurus
fact: The best-known stegosaur from China. Its spikes and plates closely resemble Stegosaurus, suggesting these features evolved early and were conserved.

name: Chungkingosaurus
fact: One of the smallest stegosaurs. Its narrow, paired spikes were arranged differently from the alternating plate pattern seen in Stegosaurus.

name: Miragaia
fact: A European stegosaur with the longest neck of any stegosaur — an unusual trait for a group otherwise known for short, heavy builds.

name: Dacentrurus
fact: The first stegosaur formally described from Europe. It had a formidable row of sharp spikes running from its back to the tip of its tail.

name: Dimorphodon
fact: An early pterosaur with a disproportionately large, puffin-like head. It was likely an agile climber of sea cliffs in early Jurassic Britain.

name: Rhamphorhynchus
fact: Preserved fossils have been found with fish in the throat. Its long tail ended in a diamond-shaped vane used as a rudder during flight.

name: Dsungaripterus
fact: Had unusual upturned jaws with a blunt, crushing tip, perfectly suited for prying shellfish and crustaceans from rocks along shorelines.

name: Tapejara
fact: A crested pterosaur from Brazil with a large, colorful sail-like crest used for display. It may have also acted as a rudder during flight.
